## Security verdict: BLOCK

PR #194, exact head `52cb3642755ca0dcd325fcafd8a029583f706b06`.

Delta review from `f4d0e45` and directly dependent source. The catalog and SidecarBg repair pass, but the required security build guard silently excludes production source. **This is a source-proven proof blocker, not a demonstrated new exploit.**

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new exploitable vulnerability demonstrated; scanner blocker below | - |

### Proof blocker: production after test declarations is never scanned

`crates/daemon/tests/notice_ids.rs:36-39` truncates each source file at the first `#[cfg(test)]` followed by a module declaration, assuming the remainder is test-only.

`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:4584-4585` begins external test declarations, not a test-only remainder. Production continues afterward, including sidecar admission and its reserved-ID guard (`:4623-4674`) and Telegram staging/queue admission (`:4725-4799`).

Those production regions never reach literal scanning or function-parameter/argument discovery. The claimed all-ID-argument enforcement therefore omits an actual security-sensitive ingress region. Exclude individual test items/modules without discarding later production, and add a regression with production code after an external test-module declaration. Confidence in this instrument defect: 10/10 from direct source inspection; no mutant was executed here.

### Repairs that pass

The macro generates enum, ALL and prefixes from one declaration (`crates/core/src/notice_id.rs:22-107`). The source-invocation oracle independently compares written names/prefixes with compiled ALL (`notice_ids.rs:379-397`), rather than deriving both sides from ALL. Dropping a generated entry is detectable; deleting an entire declaration is not independently proved by that oracle alone.

SidecarBg preserves `bg-{id}-cancelled` and `bg-{id}-terminal` bytes through the reserved helper (`crates/sidecars/src/background.rs:321,435`). Existing admission guards reserve that prefix before local/peer routing or Telegram staging (`http/mod.rs:1956,4641`). Sidecar payload/dedupe keys retain the notice ID unchanged, and queue admission checks the ledger transactionally (`crates/sidecars/src/common.rs:186-214`; `crates/store/src/queue.rs:575-629`).

The all-argument scanner handles discovered msg_id/dedupe_key positions, multiline calls and semicolon-terminated declarations (`notice_ids.rs:197-262,300-318`). Its call-shape controls use manually supplied positions, not full discovery coverage; they do not fix the truncation.

### Scope and proof limits

F146/general next_message_id remains outside this PR and uncleared. Withdrawal compatibility notes stand: old `.withdrawn` rows do not deduplicate the new key, so an upgrade-spanning retry can duplicate; the zero-old-row live-store claim was not independently checked.

Changed fixtures are synthetic; no new C19/C21 disclosure was identified. GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42524679828` and Delivers run `42524680195` both identify this SHA and success. Green CI cannot prove coverage of source discarded before the scan.

No local tests, builds, scanner/mutant execution, runtime sends, credential reads or mutations were performed.
